verdict.rationale: Lium documents an official SDK on its own developer page: it rents the cheapest matching node, runs a function there, returns the result and removes the pod. It installs via `pip install lium.io`. The live OpenAPI 3.1 schema with typed-client generation is only a supplementary building block. The 404 probe checked docs.lium.io paths, not the documented lium.io/api/openapi.json, so it does not contradict the docs. missing for 10: explicit SDK language coverage and multi-language SDKs, SDK API reference depth, independent or hands-on corroboration of SDK use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: The SDK rents the cheapest matching node, runs the function there, returns the result and removes the pod (or keeps it warm).
The Lium platform API publishes a live [OpenAPI 3.1](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0) schema.
